analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture details an automated server migration factory pattern using CloudEndure and AWS Application Discovery Service. 1. analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Cinefilm's PixelStrings video processing platform on AWS. The user accesses the platform via a Web Browser to log in and provide S3 bucket keys. The Web Server / Job Manager runs on an EC2 instance. To display media details, the Job Manager invokes AWS Lambda functions running MediaInfo to inspect video clips stored in the user's S3 bucket. Metadata retrieved by Lambda is saved to an RDS Database, which the Web Server reads to display clip attributes in the UI. When a user submits a video transformation workflow (e.g., retiming, deinterlacing, noise removal using Wormhole, Spacetime, or Dark Energy), the Job Manager coordinates with G3 GPU-accelerated EC2 instances. The G3 instances perform the processing and write the resulting media clips back to the user's S3 bucket. An IMF (Interoperable Master Format) EC2 component handles packaging for platforms like Netflix when selected in the workflow.

graph.name: American Family Group Application Modernization Architecture
graph.categories: AWS Modernization, Serverless, Strangler Fig Pattern
graph.notes: Architectural overview showing how American Family Group incrementally modernizes a legacy on-prem Tomcat application into a serverless AWS stack using API Gateway, Lambda, CloudFront, S3, and DynamoDB.

nodes.name: Independent Insurance Agents
nodes.notes: End-users accessing the single page application to sell policies.

nodes.name: CloudFront CDN
nodes.notes: Serves SPA frontend assets and routes API traffic to API Gateway.

nodes.name: S3 Static Web Hosting
nodes.notes: Stores static single page application web assets.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Acts as the API entry point for modern backend services.

nodes.name: Lambda Authorizer
nodes.notes: Executes token verification and access permission authorization.

nodes.name: Main Python Backend Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless Python execution environment hosting modernized business logic functions.

nodes.name: EC2 Legacy Tomcat App
nodes.notes: Hosts legacy Tomcat/Java application functions that have not yet been migrated.

nodes.name: DynamoDB Regional Session Store
nodes.notes: Regional DynamoDB table used to cache user session state across availability zones.

edges.notes: Agent requests single page web application.
CloudFront fetches static web content from S3 bucket.
Application routes backend API requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway triggers Lambda Authorizer to validate user access permissions.
Authorized calls are routed to the serverless Python Lambda.
Python Lambda delegates unmigrated requests to legacy Tomcat application on EC2.
Legacy Tomcat application returns data back to the serverless backend.
Python Lambda reads and updates user session cache in DynamoDB.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: 1. Identified architectural components from visual board and transcript: Drones, 3rd Party Software, CloudWatch Event, Step Functions, Lambda, S3, Storage Gateway, On-Prem Server, On-Prem Database. 2. Verified against vocabulary list: Drones maps to UserCompanyDrone, 3rd Party Software to ThirdParty, CloudWatch Event to CloudWatch, Step Functions to StepFunctions, Lambda to Lambda, S3 to S3, Storage Gateway to StorageGateway, On-Prem Server/Database to OnPremDC. 3. Modeled data and control flows into distinct sequential flows: Flow 0 for raw image capture, Flow 1 for scheduled ETL orchestration via Step Functions and Lambda, and Flow 2 for hybrid reading of S3 images via Storage Gateway. 4. Ensured output strictly adheres to JSON schema and single-line format rules.

graph.name: Marathon Oil Drone Image Processing Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture demonstrating automated drone imagery processing from third-party systems into AWS S3 using Step Functions and Lambda, integrated with on-premises mapping servers via AWS Storage Gateway.

nodes.name: Drones
nodes.notes: Flown by third-party pilots to routinely capture well pad imagery.

nodes.name: 3rd Party Software
nodes.notes: Processes imagery and generates ortho mosaic, DTM, and DEM files.

nodes.name: CloudWatch Event
nodes.notes: Triggers the Step Functions state machine on a scheduled basis.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates the sequence of Lambda functions.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes API calls to check for new images, copy them to S3, and create raster proxies.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores the processed image files.

nodes.name: Storage Gateway
nodes.notes: Enables the on-premises mapping server to read directly from S3 using standard file protocols.

nodes.name: On-Prem Server
nodes.notes: On-premises mapping software server accessed by internal operations teams.

nodes.name: On-Prem Database
nodes.notes: Local database storing raster proxy metadata and file pointers.

edges.notes: Drones upload raw imagery to third-party software.
CloudWatch Event triggers Step Functions workflow on schedule.
Step Functions orchestrates and invokes Lambda functions.
Lambda calls third-party API to check for new flight data.
Third-party software transfers image files to S3 bucket.
Lambda writes raster proxy entries into local database.
On-prem mapping server requests image files via Storage Gateway.
Storage Gateway retrieves requested files from S3.
